question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 1
question: Ownership of the Credit Risk Management Policy Guide (CPG) rests with which officer?

options.A: The Chief Risk Officer (CRO)
options.B: The Board of Trustees
options.D: The Group Head, Credit Risk Management

discussion: Selected Answer: A. Confirmed verbatim against section 1.2.
community_answer: A. The Chief Risk Officer (CRO)

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 2
question: The Board of Trustees of Access Bank has approved these policies for use bank-wide

options.A: True
options.B: False

discussion: Selected Answer: B. False – Access Bank is governed by a Board of Directors, not a Board of Trustees.
community_answer: B. False

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 3
question: The Board of Trustees will approve all changes to the CPG

options.A: True
options.B: False

discussion: Selected Answer: B. False – same reason: no Board of Trustees.
community_answer: B. False

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 4
question: The CPG guide eliminates the need for personal judgement in banking

options.A: True
options.B: False

discussion: Selected Answer: B. False – the CPG channels judgement, it does not eliminate it.
community_answer: B. False

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 5
question: If the CPG differs from applicable regulations, does the marketer (Relationship Manager) decide which approach the Bank will use?

options.A: No, since the CPG is intended to align with, not override, regulatory requirements
options.B: Yes, the marketer has full discretion to choose whichever approach favours the customer
options.C: Yes, but only for facilities below N10 million
options.D: The CPG is entirely silent on regulatory conflicts

discussion: Selected Answer: A. False as originally framed – section 2 commits to regulatory compliance, not marketer discretion.
community_answer: A. No, since the CPG is intended to align with, not override, regulatory requirements

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 6
question: Any deviations from the CPG must always be explained and justified in writing

options.A: True
options.B: False

discussion: Selected Answer: A. Consistent with the CPG's documentation-heavy approach to exceptions.
community_answer: A. True

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 7
question: The Bank may need to change the CPG's policies and procedures as laws, market conditions and the Bank's strategy change

options.A: True
options.B: False

discussion: Selected Answer: A. Confirmed – section 1.4 and 2.7 provide for periodic review and revision.
community_answer: A. True

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 8
question: The CPG may be altered or even withdrawn as the need arises; any such change must be communicated to all concerned parties

options.A: True
options.B: False

discussion: Selected Answer: A. Confirmed, consistent with version control and review framework.
community_answer: A. True

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 9
question: What is the core objective of the Credit Risk Management Policy Guide?

options.A: To maximize risk-adjusted returns through identification, measurement, limits, monitoring and reporting
options.B: To eliminate all credit risk from the Bank's balance sheet entirely
options.C: To ensure the Bank never records a single non-performing loan
options.D: To transfer all credit risk decision-making to the Central Bank of Nigeria

discussion: Selected Answer: A. Confirmed verbatim against section 2 (Core Objective).
community_answer: A. To maximize risk-adjusted returns through identification, measurement, limits, monitoring and reporting

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 10
question: Which of the following is listed among the Supporting Objectives of the CPG?

options.A: To guarantee zero credit losses under all circumstances
options.B: To restrict lending exclusively to government-backed obligors
options.C: To eliminate the Relationship Manager's role in origination
options.D: Lowest industry NPLs while maximizing returns on assets

discussion: Selected Answer: D. Confirmed against section 2's Supporting Objectives list.
community_answer: D. Lowest industry NPLs while maximizing returns on assets

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 11
question: Does the CPG's scope cover exposures in the Trading Book that are subject to market risk capital charge?

options.A: Yes, but only above N1 billion
options.B: The CPG is silent on this distinction
options.C: No, that falls under the Market Risk Policy instead
options.D: Yes, Banking and Trading Book exposures are treated equally

discussion: Selected Answer: C. Confirmed verbatim against section 2 (Scope).
community_answer: C. No, that falls under the Market Risk Policy instead

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 12
question: Preliminary screening of credit facility requests shall be completed within what timeframe of receipt of the request?

options.A: 24 calendar hours, including weekends
options.B: 1 working day

discussion: Selected Answer: B. Confirmed verbatim against section 6.2.1.
community_answer: B. 1 working day

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 13
question: Preliminary credit screening shall be the responsibility of which officer?

options.A: The relevant customer-facing market/relationship officer
options.B: The Chief Risk Officer personally, for every request regardless of size

discussion: Selected Answer: A. Confirmed against section 6.2.1.
community_answer: A. The relevant customer-facing market/relationship officer

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 14
question: If a facility request fails preliminary credit screening against the Bank's target market and risk acceptance criteria, what happens?

options.A: The request is automatically escalated to the Board Credit Committee for a second opinion
options.B: The request proceeds to full underwriting anyway, since preliminary screening is only advisory
options.C: The request is held indefinitely, without any customer communication
options.D: It is rejected then, in writing, with denial endorsed by the relevant Group Head

discussion: Selected Answer: D. Confirmed against section 6.2.1.
community_answer: D. It is rejected then, in writing, with denial endorsed by the relevant Group Head

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 15
question: Techno-Economic Viability (TEV) studies shall be conducted using which of the following?

options.A: External experts only, always
options.B: Outsourced entirely to the CBN
options.C: Internal or external experts, per project need

discussion: Selected Answer: C. CORRECTION – TEV can use internal or external experts.
community_answer: C. Internal or external experts, per project need

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 16
question: A Techno-Economic Viability (TEV) study must be carried out in which of the following cases?

options.A: TEV studies are never mandatory, only optional at the customer's own request
options.B: Whenever a new technology or the appropriate authority's own assessment demands critical feasibility analysis
options.C: Only for facilities below N10 million
options.D: Only for facilities extended to first-time individual retail customers

discussion: Selected Answer: B. Confirmed against the TEV Study guidelines.
community_answer: B. Whenever a new technology or the appropriate authority's own assessment demands critical feasibility analysis

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 17
question: External experts engaged to conduct a TEV study must meet what standard?

options.A: High repute, qualified chartered engineers/technicians in the field
options.B: No specific qualification standard, only availability
options.C: Must be employed exclusively by the CBN
options.D: Must be a serving Board Credit Committee member

discussion: Selected Answer: A. Confirmed against the TEV Study guidelines.
community_answer: A. High repute, qualified chartered engineers/technicians in the field

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 18
question: What is the purpose of Credit Audit under the CPG?

options.A: To independently re-negotiate pricing on existing facilities
options.B: To replace the annual review process entirely
options.C: To handle customer complaints about credit facility declines
options.D: To ensure appraisal standards were followed before each approval level

discussion: Selected Answer: D. Confirmed verbatim against section 6.8.
community_answer: D. To ensure appraisal standards were followed before each approval level

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 19
question: Under the current CPG, all standard borrower accounts with a limit of what amount and above, having a risk rating of 5 or better, are covered under Credit Audit?

options.A: N5 million
options.B: N100 million

discussion: Selected Answer: C. CORRECTION – section 6.8 states N10 million, not N50 million.
community_answer: C. N10 million

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 20
question: Which of the following is a factor considered when scheduling accounts for Credit Audit?

options.A: The number of dependents listed by the obligor
options.B: Exposure above N10 million, or a Risk Rating below 5
options.C: The obligor's preferred branch location only
options.D: Whether the obligor uses online banking

discussion: Selected Answer: B. Confirmed against section 6.8's factors.
community_answer: B. Exposure above N10 million, or a Risk Rating below 5

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 21
question: What is the minimum requirement for all items pledged as security for credit facilities?

options.A: A perfected legal mortgage in the name of Access Bank Plc
options.B: A simple letter of comfort from the obligor's auditors
options.D: Verbal confirmation of ownership by the obligor

discussion: Selected Answer: A. Confirmed verbatim against the collateral requirements section.
community_answer: A. A perfected legal mortgage in the name of Access Bank Plc

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 22
question: It is Access Bank policy that all credit extensions to corporate obligors shall be secured by:

options.A: A personal guarantee from a company director only
options.B: Nothing further beyond the loan agreement itself
options.C: A minimum of three trade references

discussion: Selected Answer: D. Confirmed against the collateral requirements section.
community_answer: D. An all-assets debenture

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 23
question: Is there any exception to the all-assets debenture requirement for corporate obligors?

options.A: Yes, but only for obligors owned by the Federal Government
options.B: Yes, but only for obligors with facilities below N1 million
options.C: Yes, for strongly-rated obligors with a clean 5-year default history
options.D: No, this requirement applies without exception to every corporate obligor

discussion: Selected Answer: C. Confirmed against the collateral requirements section.
community_answer: C. Yes, for strongly-rated obligors with a clean 5-year default history

question_no: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit - Question 24
question: Deviations to Policy guidelines regarding Acceptance Criteria, Techno-Economic Viability Study requirements, and Minimum Acceptable Margin Guidelines shall be approved by which body?

options.A: The Central Bank of Nigeria directly
options.B: The Board Credit Committee (BCC)
options.C: The Relationship Manager, at their own discretion
options.D: The Chief Risk Officer alone, without further escalation

discussion: Selected Answer: B. New question from the manual's list of deviations.
community_answer: B. The Board Credit Committee (BCC)
